scenes.title: Read the map as evidence
scenes.narration: Open Mapping for the fictional training department and read an actual call label before interpreting a marker. The warehouse popup identifies an incident description; it does not prove where a person or apparatus is now. This walkthrough reviews Core administration and recorded training data. Device permissions and field tracking need their own application checks. Keep the distinction visible when using the map for fire, community response, or industrial standby.

scenes.title: Review the department address and default center
scenes.narration: In Department Settings, review Address and Default Map Center GPS Coordinates. The paired latitude and longitude inputs describe the starting map view, not a live vehicle fix. This recorded example uses a fictional Chicago address and explicit decimal coordinates. Check Street, City, State/Province, Zip/Postal Code and Country before relying on the extent. Save and Cancel are visible; this demonstration only reads existing values and leaves the department unchanged.

scenes.title: Separate a station position from its response boundary
scenes.narration: Open Edit Group and confirm Station Group and Group Name before reading Station Address. Firehouse 51 has a fictional Chicago address and Gps Coordinates; the lower what3words Address field is empty. Address, coordinates or what3words are alternative station-location inputs, not proof of a live fix. Group Boundary is a separate response or service area. This demonstration reads existing values only and preserves the station, boundary, apparatus assignment and crew.

scenes.title: Recognize a station-origin estimate
scenes.narration: Open the recorded Engine 51 position popup. It explicitly says Station location and shows the station coordinates with the call location. That comparison uses a stored origin. A unit in quarters, or one without an available live position, can be measured from its station according to the configured response-origin rules. Read the source before using the estimate. The displayed distance and estimated minute are not proof of physical presence, arrival, or an active navigation route.

scenes.title: Review minute-based map TTL and status overwrite
scenes.narration: Mapping and BigBoard Settings separates personnel and unit controls. TTL In Minutes for Personnel Locations and TTL In Minutes for Unit Locations both show zero in these retained views. Zero disables ping expiry; the help text’s sixty-minute example is not a saved sixty. A location-bearing status can remain a fallback after a ping expires. The separate no-location-status checkboxes affect replacement behavior. Review the source and policy before promising that a marker will disappear.

scenes.title: Review dispatch age and response limits in seconds
scenes.narration: Closest Unit Response Tuning belongs to dispatch settings. Maximum unit location age and Maximum personnel location age are in seconds; both recorded values are eighteen hundred. They are separate from the map TTL fields measured in minutes. Include stale locations is unchecked. Maximum response radius is zero, meaning no configured maximum radius. These controls influence candidate evaluation. They do not certify a fresh device fix, prove coverage of a service area, or change the map merely because its page refreshed.
